account:
Today has seemed quiet, with no clear sign of unusual town business. I visited the market, reviewed the town accounts, attended tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage, and returned to the office before coming home at 19:07. Townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery; that sounds consistent with baking, though I did not see it myself. The treasury contained 128 emeralds when I inspected it, and I withdrew none. No separate accounting papers were supplied, and the secretary said no bills, correspondence, or waiting visitors had been brought to her attention. She recorded my treasury report and returned the accounts and appointment books to the chest.

There was some uncertainty about the tea arrangements: the secretary initially could not confirm the host or cottage, and said the cottages were unanswered and warehouse workers knew nothing. Nevertheless, I found the neighbour waiting at the dockside cottage, and we had a friendly visit. The neighbour described a quiet afternoon and asked for a meeting at town hall tomorrow at eighteen, calling it an ordinary meeting. I agreed, and the secretary recorded it in an addendum. I have not learned any further purpose for that meeting and have no evidence of a hidden one.

Tomorrow's scheduled business includes the ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill and council letters in the afternoon. The secretary has agreed to notify me if grain reports or letters arrive. I should read the appointment books in the office in the morning, including the addendum, and keep those appointments.
